transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi there, I'm Dora. I'm a clinical conversational agent and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or recovery. Do you have any questions for me today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can go back to light exercise, such as gardening, one week after surgery. However, you should avoid strenuous exercise for a month. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: If you were using eye drops for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I'm feeling very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside. However, if you have significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, that is not normal and may need further assessment. Do you have any other questions?
transcript.delivered: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It’s common for your vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation. This should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is getting significantly worse or blurrier, we may need to check it to make sure it’s okay. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all for now. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm, have all your questions been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered all my questions. I appreciate your help!
